subject: EdgeWorks Private VPC - operational accountability addendum
messages:
From: Gina Park <gina.park@edgeworks.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Private VPC – request to align operational accountability

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As EdgeWorks prepares to sign the Private deployment addendum, our networking team surfaced a couple of operational items that will affect how we can accept standard uptime/latency guarantees. Specifically: our edge transit (managed by EdgeWorks) sits upstream of the customer-side NAT and private peering; we own the NAT, some BGP session parameters, and customer-provided KMS endpoints. In the last quarter we observed three incidents where packet bursts on our transit added 120–600ms tail latency to traffic before it hit Redwood’s private gateway.

We want to propose an accountability addendum that: 1) excludes customer-controlled transit events from Redwood’s latency SLOs, 2) defines evidence required for attribution (e.g., packet captures, peering BGP dumps, timestamps), and 3) specifies monitoring hooks/metrics (SRv6/flow logs, synthetic pings) that both parties will maintain.

Can your team review and confirm whether Redwood can accept a 99.5% availability target for the Private service with a customer-infra attribution carveout documented as an appendix? If so, we can circulate a short draft and route through procurement. I attached a short sample trace bundle for context.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement has a tight timeline.

Thanks,
Gina Park
Head of Cloud Operations, EdgeWorks
attachments: network-trace-samples.zip

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Gina Park <gina.park@edgeworks.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-02T14:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Private VPC – request to align operational accountability

Hi Gina,

Thanks for flagging this and for the trace bundle — that helped clarify the tail latency pattern. We can support a customer-attribution carveout, but we need to ensure the language is operationally actionable. High level proposal:

- SLA baseline: Redwood proposes a Private availability SLA of 99.9% for service-side faults.
- Attribution carveout: events where EdgeWorks-managed transit or customer-controlled network elements (NAT, managed BGP, customer KMS endpoints) are the primary root cause will be excluded from latency/availability calculations provided EdgeWorks supplies the agreed evidence.
- Evidence & instrumentation: packet captures with synchronized timestamps (NTP/TC), BGP adjacency state dumps, router runnables and flow logs, and synthetic probe logs. We need a minimum of two corroborating artifacts to accept attribution.
- Monitoring hooks: we can provide a read-only role to the Redwood diagnostics dashboard for a narrow set of metrics (tcp_syn latency, egress queue depth, prefix reachability) and an ingest endpoint for EdgeWorks synthetic pings.
- Fallback & mitigations: where feasible Redwood will route requests to a hot-standby path or model variant to reduce customer impact; if failover increases latency beyond agreed limits, that event is classified per the same attribution rules.

I'll draft an "Operational Accountability Addendum" with a short shared-responsibility matrix and a binding evidence checklist. Can Karthik and Marissa review the proposed language below and confirm we can accept "99.5% effective availability" as the committed SLA when the carveout applies? If accepted, I'll send a docx for legal/procurement.

Proposed single-line commitment for the addendum: "Redwood warrants 99.9% availability for service-managed components. For requests routed over customer-managed transit where primary root cause is attributable to the customer network, Redwood will measure effective availability excluding attributable minutes; in these cases Redwood's effective availability commitment is 99.5%."

Alex
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
attachments: none

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-03T10:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Private VPC – request to align operational accountability

Alex / Marissa,

Quick notes from implementation perspective:

- I agree we should accept 99.5% effective availability when the carveout is invoked — that gives customers reasonable coverage while protecting Redwood from infra outside our control.
- Evidence checklist should require: (a) time-synced pcap snippet (<=10MB) showing increased egress latency, (b) BGP state snapshot around event, (c) router/switch CPU/mem counters or queue depth logs. Two of three is fine for preliminary attribution; three required for formal SLA exclusion.
- Propose to add a short operational playbook section: 1) Triage window (48 hours) for initial evidence exchange, 2) Joint RCA within 10 business days, 3) If disputed, commit to an independent traceroute/time-series review by a neutral third-party (lightweight adjudication).

I attached a first-pass draft of the addendum (edgeworks-sla-draft-v1.docx) with a responsibility matrix and example clause language. Also suggested language for morning-after monitoring hooks (synthetic pings every minute, 1m/5m summaries).

If we agree, Marissa can loop legal and procurement once Gina confirms the technical bits.

Karthik
Head of Reliability Solutions | Redwood Inference
attachments: edgeworks-sla-draft-v1.docx

From: Gina Park <gina.park@edgeworks.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@edgeworks.com
Date: 2027-08-04T16:43:00Z
Subject: Re: Private VPC – request to align operational accountability

Alex — thanks, and thanks Karthik for the quick draft.

EdgeWorks has reviewed the proposed language and we're comfortable with the 99.5% effective availability carveout, provided the evidence checklist allows us to redact limited customer PII from packet captures prior to sharing (we will provide packet headers and timestamps and a redaction hash). We also accept the 48-hour triage window and 10-business-day RCA timeline.

Next steps: please send the docx to the Redwood legal contact and share a DocuSign link when ready. Procurement would like the addendum signed within two weeks. I uploaded the trace samples and a short summary to the Jira you included.
